title: Generalized Foldy-Wouthuysen approach for the derivation of non-relativistic effective field theories
authors: Tobias Asano, Fabio Di Pumpo, Enno Giese, Motoaki Bamba
abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) are a powerful framework for performing high-precision calculations at reduced complexity compared to their fundamental counterparts. A particularly important class of EFTs arises in the non-relativistic (NR) regime. Their construction relies on a different realization of the underlying symmetries, since Lorentz invariance is no longer manifest in covariant form in the NR regime. This behavior imposes a link between certain matching coefficients, and therefore additional constraints, commonly referred to as hidden Lorentz invariance. These constraints are established in quantum field theories on inertial flat spacetime, such as NR quantum electrodynamics. However, deriving these constraints becomes considerably more involved for theories involving physics beyond the Standard Model or formulated in non-inertial spacetime backgrounds, where the hidden symmetry structure is less transparent. In this work, we present an approach to obtain the NR EFT by first constructing a relativistic EFT and then performing a generalized NR reduction based on an extended Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation. We illustrate this method by a quantum chromo-electrodynamics EFT for inertial flat spacetime, describing both electromagnetic and strong interactions, and show how it reduces to the established Lagrangian of NR quantum chromodynamics and electrodynamics. The hidden Lorentz invariance emerges as a direct consequence of the construction. This approach provides a route to obtain the NR limits of more complex theories, \eg Dirac fields in non-inertial spacetime or extensions involving physics beyond the Standard Model. As an example, we apply the method to add the coupling of a pseudoscalar axion field in a simplified model and derive its NR limit.
summary: This paper presents a generalized Foldy-Wouthuysen approach to systematically derive Non-Relativistic Effective Field Theories (EFTs). By first constructing a Lorentz-covariant relativistic EFT and then applying a generalized reduction, the authors ensure that hidden Lorentz invariance constraints are automatically incorporated. This method provides a robust tool for analyzing complex, low-energy physics in various quantum field theories.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a systematic method to derive Non-Relativistic (NR) Effective Field Theories (EFTs) for complex physical systems, especially when the underlying symmetries are difficult to track, such as in non-inertial backgrounds.
main_result: The authors propose a generalized approach involving constructing a full relativistic EFT first, followed by a generalized NR reduction using an extended Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation.
method: The method involves a two-step process: 1) Constructing a Lorentz-covariant relativistic EFT, and 2) Applying a generalized NR reduction scheme to systematically derive the low-energy, non-relativistic Lagrangian.
model_or_system: The framework is illustrated using Quantum Chromo-Electrodynamics (QCED) for inertial flat spacetime, but is claimed to be generalizable to theories involving non-Standard Model physics, such as axion couplings or Dirac fields in curved spacetime.
key_observables: The resulting Lagrangian terms, organized by powers of momentum/energy, and the emergence of hidden Lorentz invariance constraints.
important_parameters: The non-relativistic limit ($|p| \ll m$), the characteristic scale $\Lambda$ associated with heavy degrees of freedom, and the coupling constants of the underlying gauge theories (QED, QCD).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the existence of a well-defined NR limit and relies on the success of the generalized FW transformation to correctly map the relativistic structure to the non-relativistic one.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the necessity of the generalized approach, details the two-step methodology (relativistic EFT construction followed by NR reduction), applies this method to QCED to reproduce known results, and concludes by discussing its general applicability to complex theories.
why_interesting: While the focus is on particle physics EFTs, the systematic handling of symmetry breaking and scale separation via generalized transformations is a powerful theoretical tool applicable to many-body systems where low-energy effective Hamiltonians are constructed.
